title: Dual-Channel Variational Closure, Covariant Completion, and a Reproducible SPARC Benchmark
description: The dual-channel action F(x) = x^2/2 - x + ln(1+x) yields the MOND interpolation function mu(x) = x/(1+x) as its constitutive ratio F'(x)/x. Given four structural constraints (Pade[1/1] minimality, odds-ratio/Bayesian structure, the Fisher information identity F'^2 I = x^3, and dual-channel cancellation) the action is uniquely determined; the necessity of the Pade constraint is not derived and is reported as open. Embedded in the Skordis-Zlosnik RMOND framework, the linear screening ratio F''/F' = 0.004 reduces a 76x structure overproduction to 0.4%, and Vainshtein screening places the solar-system quadrupole at Q2 = 4.9e-29 s^-2, a factor 70 below the Cassini bound at natural O(1) couplings. Ghost-free with bounded Hamiltonian and c_T = c. 17 Lean 4 modules verified with no sorry and axioms restricted to {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. SPARC 175-galaxy benchmark; a0 = (1.116 +/- 14.4%) e-10 m/s^2. A pre-registered a0(z) test favours constant a0 over the horizon-tied a0(z) = xi c H(z) at 5.9 sigma, so the horizon interpretation of a0 is reported as disfavoured by our own data.
